text.p: President Bill Clinton's drug policy director on Tuesday called Mexico's arrest of its top drug-fighting official "appropriate" but expressed disappointment that corruption had reached such a high level.

Army Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, head of the national Institute for the Combat of Drugs (INCD), was fired for alleged links to Mexico's most powerful narcotics trafficker and charged with drug corruption.
U.S. National Drug Policy director Barry McCaffrey said the Mexican government had taken "the appropriate action."
"This demonstrates that Mexico is seriously threatened by corruption and violence but will take strong steps to root them out," he said in a written statement.
McCaffrey noted that the INCD was the equivalent of the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration and said that Rebollo had "a reputation as an honest and competent officer."

"We are extremely disappointed that corruption may have reached such a level in Mexico .... Mexico is taking the right action. Faced with evidence indicating serious wrongdoing, they are acting to determine the truth of their information," McCaffrey said.
"We support the actions the government of Mexico has taken to date and urge them to pursue their investigation," he added.

Gutierrez, 62, was appointed to his job only two months ago. He disappeared from public view last week and Mexican officials said Monday that he was in a military hospital after suffering a heart attack Feb. 7.
